How do you want it done?

What does it need?

Your fixed price

Choose your mechanic. Each sets their own hourly rate.

Budget: lowest-price parts. Standard: trusted brands, the choice most people make. Premium: the same quality as the car maker’s own parts.

Parts matched to your car and listed from the parts supplier. Sample prices shown.

Not sure it is the right job? Your mechanic checks the car first. If it needs something different, they tell you the new price and wait for your OK before doing any extra work.

Full valet

Exterior wash and wax, plus a full interior clean. One fixed price for your vehicle size.

Includes exterior hand wash and wax, wheels and tyres, windows, interior vacuum, dashboard and trims, seats and carpets. About 3 hours.

Bodywork and alloy wheels

Mobile repairers come to you. Body shops and wheel centres do the work at their premises. Every repairer is checked, and you can choose insurance-approved repairers.

Each door, wing, bumper, the bonnet and the boot counts as one part. Repairers call these panels.

Check with your insurer before the repair. Most insurers have their own approved repairers, and you usually pay your excess (the part of any claim you pay yourself) to the repairer when you collect the car.

One close-up and one from a few steps back, in daylight if you can.

Guide prices only. Each repairer sends you a fixed price from your photos, usually within 24 hours. You pay nothing until you accept a quote.

Not sure? Most wheels are painted one colour all over. Diamond-cut wheels have a bright metal face with fine lines, like the back of a CD.

Mobile tyre fitting

A fitter comes to you with the tyres on the van.

Budget: the lowest price. Mid-range: well-known makes, the choice most people make. Premium: the top makes, with the best grip in the wet and the longest life. Your fitter brings the right size for your car.

Sample prices shown for the preview.

Why book through The Motoring Central?

Eight reasons drivers use us instead of ringing round.

Only vetted local traders

Every partner sends us their trade insurance, public liability insurance and photo ID before they can take a single booking.

A fixed price before you book

See the full price up front, including our booking fee. No call-out surprises and nothing added on the day without your say.

Compare in one place

Prices, distance, ratings and reviews for local partners side by side, so you can choose who you trust instead of ringing round.

Reviews you can believe

Only customers with a completed booking can leave a review, and we publish the good and the bad alike.

Kept in the loop

Confirmation by email and text, a reminder the day before, an alert when your partner is on the way, and a chat line to them.

A UK team behind you

If anything is not right, message or call our UK support team and we will step in and help sort it out with the partner.

Pay safely online

Card payments are handled by a regulated payment provider. We never see or store your full card number.

Everything in one account

Save your vehicles in My garage, get MOT reminders, and book a mechanic, tyres, a valet or recovery from the same place.

How MOT pricing works

If you also test MOTs, they work differently from repairs. Customers pay the official DVSA maximum fee when they book online, with nothing added on top. We pay you all of it except a flat £5 booking fee per MOT, which we keep (it includes VAT).

TestCustomer paysPaid to you
Car, up to 8 passenger seats (class 4)£54.85£49.85
Motorcycle (class 1 and 2)£29.65£24.65
Goods vehicle 3,000 to 3,500kg (class 7)£58.60£53.60
More than 16 passenger seats (class 5)£80.65£75.65
  • A flat £5 booking fee per online MOT, and no monthly fee. MOTs are not part of the 10% fee, which only covers repairs and servicing
  • Paid weekly, straight to your bank
  • You choose which MOT classes you test, and customers only see you for those
  • Online bookings go straight into your free live diary
  • Free to join: no joining fee and no contract
  • Tick "We also do MOT tests" on the form below to add MOTs to your garage

Paid to you each month (car MOTs)

MOT test stations: see how online booking fills your bays

One fair price at every partner, £49.85 paid to you per car MOT, bookings 24/7 and a free live diary. About 1 minute 40.

MOT test station. Choose the classes you are authorised to test. We pay you the official fee less a £5 booking fee for each one. Customers only see you for the classes you tick.

Each bay becomes a column in your free booking diary. You can add, rename or remove bays later.

MOT classes you test, and what we pay you

The site number on your DVSA authorisation. We check it against the DVSA list of MOT test stations.

Tick each type of test your station is authorised for. We pay you the official fee less a flat £5 booking fee for every MOT booked online, shown next to each test (£49.85 for a car MOT). Nothing else is taken from it, and the customer pays in full when they book. Bookings go straight into your free live diary, and your own walk-ins and phone bookings close those times online.

What is a premium ad?

Your car or van appears in the revolving banner on the front page. Each premium ad runs for 2 weeks or until the car sells, whichever comes first. Free premium ads reset each month and do not roll over. Extra premium ads are £5.00 + VAT each (launch offer, usually £9.99 + VAT). All dealer prices are plus VAT.

Vehicle history checks. Every car and van you list is checked for outstanding finance, insurance write-off and stolen records when you publish it, and any write-off is shown clearly on the advert. Each plan includes a number of checks a month, and extra checks are £3.50 + VAT each. Your 30-day free trial includes 3 checks. After those, during the trial the check is your choice: pay £3.50 + VAT for it, or list for free without one. An advert without a check is marked “Not history checked”, and buyers can still see its MOT history and the mileage recorded at each test, free from the DVSA.

Terms and conditions

Who is responsible for what when you book work, buy a vehicle or join Motoring Central as a partner or dealer.

Draft for review. These terms are a working draft for the preview site. Have them checked by a solicitor before launch. Bracketed items such as [company number] still need filling in.

The short version

  • Motoring Central is a marketplace. We introduce you to independent garages, mobile mechanics, body shops, alloy wheel specialists, recovery companies, tyre fitters, valeters and dealers. We do not carry out the work or sell the vehicles ourselves.
  • Work and repairs: your contract is with the garage or partner who does the work. They are responsible for the quality of their work, any parts they supply, and their warranty.
  • Car and van sales: your contract is with the dealer. The dealer is responsible for the vehicle, its description, its condition and any warranty.
  • Your legal rights stay in place. Nothing in these terms takes away your rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. You use those rights against the partner or dealer you dealt with.
  • Before you book or contact a dealer, we show you who you are dealing with and ask you to confirm you understand this.

Tap a section to read it in full.

1. Using Motoring Central (all customers)

Who we are

Motoring Central is run by [The Motoring Central Ltd], a company registered in England and Wales, company number [company number], registered office [address]. Contact us at [email].

Our role

We run an online marketplace. We list independent businesses (“partners” and “dealers”). We call them partners because they work with us, but they are separate businesses: this is not a legal partnership, joint venture or agency. We show their prices and availability, and take bookings and payments for them. We are not a party to the contract for the work or the sale. Each listing and booking shows the business you are dealing with.

Who is responsible for the work or vehicle

The partner or dealer is responsible for the work they carry out, the parts and goods they supply, the vehicles they sell, and any warranty or guarantee they give. If something goes wrong, your claim is against them. We will help you contact them and, if needed, give you their full business details.

Your statutory rights

Services must be carried out with reasonable care and skill, and goods and vehicles must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described. These rights come from the Consumer Rights Act 2015 and cannot be removed by these terms. You use them against the partner or dealer.

Checks we carry out

We check each partner’s photo ID, trade insurance and public liability insurance before they can take bookings, and again when documents expire. These checks help keep the marketplace safe, but they are not a guarantee of the quality of any work.

Prices, payment and our booking fee

Prices are set by each partner. When you pay through Motoring Central, we collect the payment on the partner’s behalf, and paying us counts as paying them. Our booking fee [currently £8.33 plus VAT, which is £9.99, per booking] is shown including VAT before you book. If the partner cancels, we refund the booking fee. MOT tests work differently: the price is the official maximum fee for the class, the same at every partner test centre, with our booking fee included in it and nothing extra to pay. For MOT tests we take your payment ourselves and pay the test centre (see MOT classes and fees).

Cancelling a booking

You can cancel free of charge up to [24 hours] before the booked time. If you cancel later, the partner may charge a cancellation fee shown at the time of booking. Recovery jobs that are already under way cannot be cancelled free of charge.

Problems and complaints

Contact the partner or dealer first, using the details in your booking or the advert. If you cannot resolve it, or your complaint is about us, follow our complaints procedure (section 14 and the Complaints page). This does not affect your right to take the matter further.

Our responsibility to you

We are responsible for running the website and app with reasonable care and skill, and for the accuracy of information we write ourselves. We are not responsible for the work, parts, goods or vehicles supplied by partners or dealers. Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot be limited by law.

Reviews

Reviews must be honest and about a real booking or purchase. We may remove reviews that are false, offensive or unlawful.

Law

These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales. If you live in Scotland or Northern Ireland, you can also bring proceedings in your local courts.

2. Garages, mobile mechanics, auto electricians and locksmiths

These terms apply when you book a service, repair, diagnostic or electrical job or vehicle key or lock job with a garage, mobile mechanic, auto electrician or vehicle locksmith. Wherever this section says “garage or mechanic”, it includes auto electricians and vehicle locksmiths.

Your contract is with the garage or mechanic

The garage or mechanic named in your booking carries out the work and is responsible for it.

Warranty

The warranty on the workmanship and on any parts fitted is given by the garage or mechanic, not by Motoring Central. They must show their warranty terms before you book. Warranty claims are made directly to them. Parts carry the manufacturer’s warranty, which the garage or mechanic will deal with for you.

Extra work

If the garage or mechanic finds more work is needed, they must explain it and get your agreement and a price before doing it. You do not have to pay for extra work you did not agree to.

Mobile work

For mobile bookings you must make sure the vehicle is somewhere it is safe and legal to work on, and that you have permission to have work done there. If the job cannot be done safely, the mechanic may rearrange it.

Damage

The garage or mechanic is responsible for any damage they cause to your vehicle or property while working on it, and must hold insurance to cover this.

3. MOT tests

MOT tests are carried out by DVSA-authorised test centres listed on Motoring Central. The test result is the test centre’s decision. If you disagree with a result, raise it with the test centre first; you can also appeal to the DVSA. Any repairs after the test are a separate job with the garage, with its own price and warranty from that garage.

MOT classes and fees

The MOT you need depends on your vehicle: its class is set by the type of vehicle, its seats and its weight. Choose the right class when you book. If the test centre finds your vehicle is in a different class, they will tell you the correct fee before testing. The price shown for each class is the maximum fee set by the DVSA for that class. Our booking fee is included in that price: there is nothing extra to pay to book.

Booking times and payment

Online MOT bookings are taken from the test centre’s live diary, so the time you choose is held for you in that diary as soon as you pay. You pay the full price when you book. The Motoring Central takes your full payment and pays the test centre a fixed fee for each test. You and the test centre both get a confirmation by email and text. To move your MOT to another time, ask the test centre: they can move it in their diary and you get a new confirmation. To cancel, contact us so your payment can be refunded.

4. Tyre fitting

The tyre fitter named in your booking supplies and fits the tyres and is responsible for the fitting work and its warranty. Tyres carry the manufacturer’s warranty, which the fitter will deal with for you. Puncture repairs are only carried out where the tyre can be safely repaired; if it cannot, the fitter will tell you and offer a replacement. Follow the fitter’s advice on rechecking wheel nuts after fitting.

5. Valeting

The valeter named in your booking carries out the valet and is responsible for their work and any damage they cause. Please remove valuables before the valet. Report any problem or damage to the valeter within [48 hours], with photos if you can, so they can put it right.

6. Bodywork and alloy wheels

Your contract is with the repairer

The body shop, smart repairer or wheel specialist you choose carries out the work and is responsible for it, including any damage they cause while your vehicle is in their care.

Quotes from photos

Bodywork quotes are based on the photos and details you send. If the repairer finds more damage once they see the vehicle, they must explain it and agree a new price with you before doing extra work. You do not have to pay for work you did not agree to.

Warranty

The warranty on the repair, paintwork and alloy finish is given by the repairer, not by Motoring Central. They must show their warranty terms before you book. Paint is matched as closely as possible, but small differences in shade can occur on older or faded paint.

Insurance claims

If you are claiming on insurance, the claim is between you and your insurer. Check with your insurer before the repair. “Insurance approved” means the repairer has told us, and we have checked, that they are on at least one insurer or accident management panel. It does not mean your own insurer will accept them.

Alloy wheels

Wheels with cracks, buckles or corrosion may need straightening or may not be safe to refurbish. The specialist will tell you before starting. Check wheel nuts are tight after the work, as advised by the specialist.

7. Recovery, breakdown and mobile EV charging

For mobile EV charging, the charging company named in your booking is responsible for connecting and charging your vehicle safely with suitable, tested equipment. The price covers the call-out and the charge you chose. Follow the operator’s safety instructions at the roadside.

The recovery company named in your booking carries out the recovery and is responsible for your vehicle from when they load it until they deliver it. They must hold insurance for vehicles in their care. Prices are based on the details you give; if the job turns out to be different (for example a longer distance or extra equipment), the company must tell you the new price before carrying on. Please remove valuables, and always follow the driver’s safety instructions at the roadside.

The same applies when you book a recovery partner to deliver a car or van you have bought. Delivery is a separate booking with the recovery partner. Make sure the vehicle is paid for and the seller has agreed the collection before the delivery day.

How the price is worked out

You see each company’s full price before you book. For recovery it is the call-out fee and price per mile of the company’s most suitable truck for your vehicle (some companies include the first few miles in the call-out), plus any extras your answers make certain, for example dollies for a vehicle whose wheels will not turn, winching off the road, accident damage, a fluid spill or an out-of-hours call. Each company’s other extras are listed with their prices before you book, as “only if needed”.

Driving lessons

Driving lessons are given by independent driving instructors, who set their own prices. Every instructor we list holds a DVSA approved driving instructor (ADI) registration or a DVSA trainee licence, and we show which. You pay the instructor’s price and no booking fee. A block of hours or an intensive course is paid for in full when you book it: you book the first lesson then, and the remaining hours from your account. You can cancel or move a lesson free of charge up to [48 hours] before it starts: the hours go back to your block, or a single lesson is refunded. If you cancel later than that, or do not turn up, the lesson is charged. If your instructor cancels, you are not charged for that lesson. Unused hours in a block can be refunded: contact us. You must hold a valid provisional licence and bring it to your lessons, and you must be fit to drive.

Extras on the day

If, when they arrive, the recovery company finds that special equipment or extra work is needed that was not in your price, they must tell you what it is, why it is needed and the price (from the list you saw when booking), and get your approval before carrying on: either your signature on their device or your approval in My account. An extra is only added to your booking once you approve and pay it. If you say no, they must not carry out or charge for it, and you can agree what happens next with them or with us. Please give accurate answers when you book: if the job is very different from what you told us, the company may decline it. For mobile EV charging it is the company’s call-out charge, which includes the charge, plus their price per mile if you are outside their usual area. Distances are worked out from the postcodes or the location you give us. We add a booking fee, shown separately. You pay the total when you book.

Cancelling

You can cancel in My account free of charge until the company sets off, and you get a full refund. Once they are on their way, you can still cancel, but their call-out fee is not refunded (it is paid to them for the journey); the rest is refunded. Once they have reached you and started, the booking cannot be cancelled online. If the company cannot do the job, they hand it back before setting off and you get a full refund. Refunds go back to the card you paid with, usually within 3 to 5 working days.

Emergencies

If you or anyone else is in danger, call 999 first. On a motorway, leave the vehicle by the left-hand doors and wait behind the barrier. Booking through us is not an emergency service and arrival times are estimates.

Selling your own car or van (private sellers)

Who can place a private advert

Private adverts are for people selling their own car or van, or one they have the owner’s permission to sell. A business that is not a motor trader can also advertise a vehicle it owns, and can show the price plus VAT if it is VAT registered; its advert is marked as a business sale. Private adverts are not for motor traders. Anyone who buys and sells vehicles for profit must join as a dealer. You can have up to 3 private adverts running at once.

What you pay

A private advert costs £29.99 including VAT and runs for 30 days. A premium advert costs a further £14.99 and is shown on the front-page banner for 2 weeks or until the car is sold. The banner is shared with other premium adverts and shows them in turn, as described in section 13, so we cannot promise a position or a number of views. We charge no commission. You pay before you enter your registration, because the registration look-up and the vehicle history check cost us money to run. Fees are not refunded if the car sells early or you remove the advert.

Vehicle history check

Every advert includes one vehicle history check for outstanding finance, insurance write-off and stolen records. Your payment covers one vehicle: the check is run on the registration you confirm, and that registration cannot be changed afterwards or used for a different vehicle. The result is shown on your advert and you cannot change or remove it.

We will not publish an advert for a vehicle that the check shows has been reported stolen, has been scrapped, or is a Category A or B write-off. If the check shows outstanding finance, we will not publish the advert until the finance has been paid off and you have sent us proof, for example the settlement letter. In any of these cases, contact us: we will refund your payment less an admin fee of £9.99 including VAT, which covers the cost of the history check, or publish your advert once the finance is cleared (no admin fee). Any insurance write-off (Category S, N, C or D) is shown clearly on your advert, whether you told us about it or the check found it.

The check uses data from third parties and we cannot guarantee it is complete or correct. If you think a result is wrong, contact us.

If you do not finish your advert

If you pay but leave before your advert is published, it stays saved on the device and browser you used, and you can carry on from where you stopped for up to 6 days after paying. After that, the payment can no longer be used for an advert: contact us within 14 days of paying and we will refund it in full if the history check has not been run, or less the £9.99 admin fee (including VAT) if it has.

Your advert

You are responsible for your advert. It must be honest and accurate, including the mileage, condition, history and any faults you know about. You must be legally able to sell the car. You must answer honestly whether it has ever been an insurance write-off. We can remove any advert that is misleading, breaks these terms or is reported and found to be a problem.

Checking your advert before it goes live

We check every advert before buyers can see it, usually within a few hours. Some checks are automatic and some are done by our team. Your 30 days (and any premium banner time) start when your advert goes live, not when you send it. If we do not approve your advert, we tell you why so you can fix it and send it back. If it cannot be fixed, contact us within 14 days and we will refund your payment less the £9.99 admin fee (including VAT) that covers the history check. If we decline an advert because we believe it is a scam or deliberately misleading, we do not refund it.

The sale

The sale is a private agreement between you and the buyer. Motoring Central is not a party to it, does not inspect the car and does not handle the payment for the car.

8. Buying a car or van

Your contract is with the dealer

Cars and vans on Motoring Central are advertised and sold by independent dealers. Any sale, deposit, part exchange, finance or delivery is agreed between you and the dealer. Motoring Central does not own, inspect or sell the vehicles.

Liability and warranty stay with the dealer

The dealer is responsible for the advert being accurate, for the vehicle’s condition, history and roadworthiness, for making sure they have the right to sell it, and for any warranty they offer. Any claim about the vehicle is made against the dealer.

Your rights

When you buy from a dealer, the vehicle must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described. If it is faulty you may have the right to reject it within 30 days, or to a repair or replacement after that. If you buy without visiting the dealer, you may also have cancellation rights. These rights are against the dealer. Vans bought for business use have fewer consumer rights.

Before you buy

We recommend you view and test drive the vehicle, check the V5C and service history, and run a vehicle history check before paying a deposit.

9. Partner terms (garages, mechanics, body shops, wheel specialists, recovery, tyres, valeting)

Independent business

You join Motoring Central as an independent business. We call you a “partner”, but this does not create a legal partnership or joint venture, and you are not our employee or agent.

Driving instructors

You must hold a current DVSA ADI registration or trainee licence for as long as you take bookings, display your badge as the law requires, and tell us straight away if it lapses, is suspended or changes. Your tuition car must have dual controls, be roadworthy, taxed and MOT’d where needed, and be insured for driving tuition for payment. You set your own hourly rate and any discounts. We collect the learner’s payment on your behalf and pay you for each lesson, less our fee of [10%] plus VAT; hours in a block are paid to you as each lesson is booked and given. A learner may cancel free of charge up to [48 hours] before a lesson; later than that you are still paid for it. If you cancel a lesson you are not paid for it. Keep your diary up to date: learners can book any time shown as free.

Recovery prices and extras

Recovery partners quote from the fleet and price list they keep on their dashboard, and must keep it accurate. An extra that is not in the customer’s booked price may only be added through the site, at the price shown to the customer when they booked (or a clear price for anything else), and only after the customer has approved it by signing on your device or approving online. Do not use the equipment or carry out that work before approval. Extras that were not approved cannot be charged.

Complaints

If we pass you a customer complaint, you must reply to us within [5 working days] with your account, any records of the job (inspection, photos, service sheet) and what you offer to put it right, and work with us in good faith to resolve it (see section 14).

Your work, your warranty

You are solely responsible for the quality and safety of your work, the parts and goods you supply, and any damage you cause. You give the warranty on your work and must show your warranty terms to customers before they book. You must deal with warranty claims and complaints directly, promptly and fairly, and meet customers’ rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015.

Insurance and documents

You must hold trade insurance and public liability insurance at all times (and, for recovery, cover for vehicles in your care), and keep the copies on Motoring Central in date. We may pause your account if a document expires.

Working properly

You must have the skills, qualifications and authorisations the work needs (for example DVSA authorisation for MOT tests), follow the law, dispose of waste such as oil, tyres, paint and solvents legally, follow HSE rules for spraying 2K paints, only describe yourself as insurance approved if you are on an insurer or accident management panel, and get the customer’s agreement before doing extra work.

Fees and payment

We charge a flat fee of [10%] plus VAT on each completed job. There is no monthly fee, membership or sign-up fee. The customer pays our booking fee separately; it never comes out of your price. We pay you what customers paid, less our fee, every week. MOT tests are paid differently (see MOT tests below). Trade listings are [£9.99 plus VAT] each. All our fees to partners, including the per-job fee, are exclusive of VAT, which is added at the rate in force. [VAT treatment of the per-job fee: to be confirmed with our accountant.]

MOT tests

For MOT tests booked through Motoring Central, the customer pays us the official maximum fee for the class, in full, when they book. Every partner test centre charges the same price. We pay you that fee less a flat booking fee of £5 for every test you carry out (for example £49.85 for a car, class 4). We keep the £5, which includes VAT. The amount for each class is shown when you join and in your dashboard, and is not negotiated. Our 10% fee is not charged on MOT tests. MOT test stations (MOT testing only) pay no monthly fee and no joining fee. Online MOT bookings go straight into your live diary. You may move a booking when the customer asks, and we tell the customer the new time. To cancel a paid booking, contact us so the customer can be refunded.

Indemnity

You agree to cover any loss, claim or cost we suffer because of your work, your goods or your breach of these terms.

Customer information

Use customer details only to carry out the booking, and keep them secure in line with data protection law.

Ending the agreement

You can close your account at any time. We may suspend or close accounts for poor service, missing documents or breaking these terms.

10. Dealer terms

You are the seller

You sell vehicles directly to buyers. Motoring Central provides advertising and does not take part in the sale.

Checking adverts

We check every advert before buyers can see it, usually within a few hours. Some checks are automatic and some are done by our team. If we do not approve an advert, we tell you why so you can fix it and send it back. An advert waiting for approval or not approved still counts towards your plan’s advert limit until you remove it.

Complaints

If we pass you a buyer’s complaint, you must reply to us within [5 working days] with your account and what you offer to put it right, and work with us in good faith to resolve it (see section 14). Premium ads work as described in section 13.

Liability and warranty

You are solely responsible for your adverts being accurate and complete, for each vehicle’s condition, history, roadworthiness and legal title (including no outstanding finance), for any warranty you give, and for buyers’ rights under consumer law, including returns and rejections. You must deal with complaints and claims directly.

Trading properly

You must make clear you are a business seller, hold motor trade insurance, and hold any authorisation needed for finance you offer (for example from the Financial Conduct Authority). Remove adverts promptly once a vehicle is sold or reserved.

Fees

New dealers get a free trial of [30] days on any plan from the day they are approved, including the free premium ads and [3] vehicle history checks. One free trial is allowed per dealership: if the same business (by email, phone number, or business name and town) has had a free trial before, including under another account, membership is charged from the day it is approved. The first payment is taken when the trial ends, and we email a reminder [7] days before. You can cancel during the trial and pay nothing. After that, membership is charged monthly by plan, with VAT added to every price: Starter (1 to 10 cars) [£169] with [5] vehicle history checks a month, Standard (11 to 20 cars) [£229] with [10] checks and [1] free premium ad a month, Plus (21 to 30 cars) [£299] with [15] checks and [3], Pro (31 to 50 cars) [£379] with [25] checks and [4], and Premier (51 or more cars) [£449] with [25] checks and [5]. Every vehicle listed is history checked when it is published, except that during the free trial the dealer may choose to list a vehicle without a check. Such an advert is marked “Not history checked” for its whole life, and the dealer must still declare whether the vehicle has been an insurance write-off. Checks beyond the monthly allowance, and checks beyond the [3] included in the free trial, are [£3.50] + VAT each. Unused checks do not roll over. A premium ad runs for 2 weeks or until the car sells, whichever comes first. Free premium ads do not roll over. Extra premium ads are [£5.00 plus VAT] each (usually [£9.99 plus VAT]). Trade listings: [5] free a month, then [£9.99 plus VAT] each.

Yearly plans and founding dealers

Instead of paying monthly, a dealer can pay for a year in advance at any time: [9] months of their plan price for [12] months of membership. The first [30] dealers approved (“founding dealers”) pay [8] months for [12], and get [5] free premium ads a month from approval until [2] months after their free trial ends (each runs 2 weeks or until the vehicle sells; unused ads do not roll over). A dealer keeps a founding place only if they stay past the free trial: cancelling during the trial releases the place, which goes to the next dealer approved, and it is given back on keeping the membership before the trial ends only if a place is still free. A yearly plan starts when the free trial ends (or on the day it is bought, if later). Yearly plans are not refunded if the dealer changes their mind; if we stop providing the service, we refund the months not used.

Cancelling

During the free trial you can cancel at any time, from your dashboard, and pay nothing. Cancelling during the trial takes effect immediately: your account is closed and your adverts are taken down straight away, and the free trial cannot be used again. After the trial, monthly plans need one month’s notice: your membership and adverts end one month after you cancel, and that month is charged. Yearly plans end when the paid year ends.

Vehicle registration look-ups

When you add a vehicle to your stock, you can use our registration look-up to fill in its details, free of charge, or type the details in yourself. Look-up details come from official and third-party records: check them before you advertise, as you are responsible for your adverts being accurate.

Look-up details come from third-party vehicle data providers and may be incomplete or out of date. You must check them before you save or advertise a vehicle, and you remain responsible for your adverts being accurate. Use look-ups only for vehicles you hold or are considering as stock; you must not resell the data or run look-ups in bulk by automated means. We may change the price by giving at least [30 days’] notice.

Indemnity

You agree to cover any loss, claim or cost we suffer because of your vehicles, your adverts or your breach of these terms.

11. Trade sales (trade to trade, sold as seen)

Who can use it

The Trade section is only for logged-in partners and dealers buying and selling as businesses. Private buyers cannot use it.

Sold as seen, no warranty

Every vehicle in the Trade section is sold as seen, trade to trade, with no warranty from the seller or from Motoring Central. Business buyers do not have the consumer rights that private buyers have. The buyer must inspect the vehicle and rely on their own checks.

Honest descriptions

Sellers must describe vehicles accurately, list all known faults, and have the right to sell them. A vehicle sold as seen must still match its description.

Prices and offers

Sellers either set a minimum price, which a buyer can accept straight away, or invite offers with a hidden minimum. Offers below the minimum are declined automatically. When a seller accepts an offer or a buyer buys at the minimum price, the two businesses agree payment and collection directly. Motoring Central is not a party to the sale.

Listing fees

Each trade listing is [£9.99 plus VAT]. Dealers get [5] free trade listings each calendar month with their membership. Fees are not refunded if a listing is withdrawn.

12. Job adverts

Who can advertise

Partners and dealers in the Motoring Central network can advertise vacancies at their own business. Each advert costs [£9.99 plus VAT] and runs for [90] days. The fee is paid when the advert is posted and is not refunded if the advert is removed early or the vacancy is filled.

The employer is responsible

The business that posts the advert is the employer. It is responsible for the advert being accurate, for its recruitment decisions and for any employment or contract that follows. Motoring Central is not a recruitment agency or employment business, does not vet applicants, and is not a party to any employment.

What adverts must do

Adverts must be for a genuine, current vacancy, state the pay honestly, meet the National Minimum Wage, and must not discriminate on any characteristic protected by the Equality Act 2010. Adverts must not ask applicants for money. We may edit or remove adverts that break these rules.

Applicants

Searching and applying is free. Your application is passed to the employer you apply to, who must use it only to consider you for the vacancy and handle it in line with data protection law.

13. Premium ads and the front-page banner

What a premium ad is

A premium ad puts a car or van in the front-page banner of the site and gives it a “Featured” label for [2 weeks] or until the vehicle is sold or the advert is removed, whichever comes first. Premium ads are included in some dealer plans, given to founding dealers, or bought separately by dealers and private sellers.

The banner is shared

All premium ads that are running share the banner and are shown in turn. At the moment one vehicle is shown at a time for about [4] seconds, and the order is shuffled after every round so no advertiser is always first or last. How often a vehicle appears depends on how many premium ads are running at the same time and on how long each visitor stays on the page. For example, with [30] premium ads running a vehicle comes round about every [2] minutes, and with [150] about every [10] minutes. The banner pauses while a visitor holds the pointer over it or the page is in the background.

No guaranteed position, views or results

A premium ad gives your vehicle a place in the rotation. It does not guarantee a position, a number of appearances, views, clicks, enquiries or a sale, or how often any one visitor sees it.

We may change how the banner works

To keep it working well for buyers and advertisers, we may change the banner’s design and rotation, for example by showing several vehicles at once on larger screens, changing the time each vehicle is shown, or limiting how many premium ads run at once and placing others in a short queue. Any change applies to all advertisers equally. A premium ad that is queued starts its [2 weeks] when it first appears.

Refunds

Because the banner is shared and rotates as described here, we do not give refunds or credits because of how often a vehicle appeared, its position, or the number of views or enquiries it received. If a premium ad you paid for did not appear at all because of a fault on our side, tell us within [14 days] and we will run it again or refund it. Included and free premium ads have no cash value and do not roll over.

Content

Premium ads must meet the same rules as any advert. We may remove a premium ad that breaks our terms, without a refund.

14. Complaints procedure

Who to contact first

If your complaint is about work carried out or a vehicle sold by a partner or dealer, contact them first: they are responsible for it. If it is not resolved, or your complaint is about us, complain to us using the form on our Complaints page, by phone, by email with “Complaint” in the subject, or by post.

Our timescales

We confirm receipt straight away with a reference number, contact you within [2 working days], and send a full written response within [14 days]. If we need longer, we tell you why and when to expect it, and we send our final response within [8 weeks].

Partners and dealers must help

When we pass a complaint to a partner or dealer, they must reply to us within [5 working days] with their account, any records (such as the vehicle inspection, photos or service sheet), and what they offer to put it right, and must work with us in good faith to resolve it.

Review

If you are not happy with our response, you can ask for it to be reviewed by the owner of the business, who will send a final written response within [14 days].

Help from outside

You can get free advice from the Citizens Advice consumer service (0808 223 1133), ask your card provider about a chargeback or Section 75 claim, contact The Motor Ombudsman if the dealer is accredited by them, or use the small claims court. Complaints about personal information can be made to the Information Commissioner’s Office. [We are not currently a member of an alternative dispute resolution scheme.] This procedure does not affect your legal rights.

Records

We keep a record of each complaint and how it was handled for [3 years], to deal with any follow-up and to improve our service.

Complaints procedure

If something has gone wrong, we want to hear about it and help put it right. Here is how it works and how long each step takes.

Who to talk to first

About a job, a repair or a vehicle you bought: the partner or dealer did the work or sold the vehicle, so they are responsible for putting it right. Contact them first using the details in your booking or the advert. If it is not sorted within a few days, or they do not reply, tell us and we will step in.

About us: our website, a payment or refund, our fees, our team, or how we handled something. Come straight to us.

How to make a complaint

Use the form below, or call us on 020 8191 4290, email hello@motoringcentral.co.uk with “Complaint” in the subject, or write to us at the address at the bottom of this page. Tell us what happened, your booking reference or the registration, and what you would like us to do.

We use these details to deal with your complaint and keep a record of it. See our privacy policy.

What happens next

  1. Straight away: we email you to confirm we have your complaint, with a reference number (it starts CMP).
  2. Within [2 working days]: a member of our team contacts you to understand what happened. If it is about a partner or dealer, we ask them for their side. They must reply to us within [5 working days].
  3. Within [14 days]: we send you our full response in writing, saying what we found and what we will do.
  4. If we need longer (for example, to get an inspection or a report), we tell you why and when you will hear from us. We always send our final response within [8 weeks].

If you are not happy with our response

Reply to our response, quoting your reference, and ask for a review. The owner of the business, who was not involved in the first response, looks at your complaint again and sends you a final written response within [14 days].

Help from outside

  • Citizens Advice consumer service: free advice on your rights, on 0808 223 1133 or at citizensadvice.org.uk.
  • Your card provider: if you paid by card, you may be able to ask your bank for a chargeback. For credit card payments between £100 and £30,000, Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act may also help.
  • Buying from a dealer: if the dealer is accredited by The Motor Ombudsman, you can also take your complaint to them, at themotorombudsman.org.
  • The small claims court: for claims up to £10,000 in England and Wales, through Money Claim Online on gov.uk.
  • Your personal information: you can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

[We are not currently a member of an alternative dispute resolution scheme. Confirm before launch.] Making a complaint does not affect your legal rights.

Partners and dealers

If you are a partner or dealer and you are unhappy with us, for example about a payout, a fee, your plan or a decision we made about your account, use the same form or the chat in your dashboard. The same steps and timescales apply.

Our promise

We treat every complaint fairly and in confidence, we do not charge for making one, and making a complaint never affects how we treat you. We keep a record of each complaint and what we did for [3 years], and we use them to improve our service.

Frequently asked questions

Straight answers about prices, booking, who does the work and what happens if something goes wrong.

No questions match that. Try another word, or contact us.

How it works

What is Motoring Central?

Motoring Central is one place for everything your car or van needs. You can book a mobile mechanic, garage, MOT, auto electrician or locksmith, tyre fitter, valeter, body shop or alloy wheel specialist, recovery and mobile EV charging, and browse cars and vans for sale from dealers.

We are a marketplace. The work is done by independent local businesses that we check before they can take a booking.

How do I get a price?

Choose the service and the job on the home page and you will see what it costs from, with no sign-up. Then register free and enter your registration once: we run a full vehicle check and show the exact fixed price for your vehicle from local partners.

Is the price fixed?

Yes. You see the full price, including parts, labour and our booking fee, before you book. If the partner finds extra work is needed, they must explain it and agree a price with you before doing it.

What is the booking fee?

We charge a small booking fee on each booking. It is shown before you book. It is [£9.99] per booking including VAT (£8.33 plus VAT). If the partner cancels, we refund the booking fee.

Can I choose who does the work?

Yes. You compare partners by price, rating and distance, and pick the one you want. Each partner sets their own prices.

Do you cover my area?

We are building our network across the UK. Enter your registration and postcode and we will show the partners available near you. If nobody covers your area yet, tell us and we will let you know when that changes.

Booking and paying

How do I pay?

You pay by card through our secure checkout when you book. We collect the payment on the partner’s behalf and pass it on to them. We do not store your full card details.

Can I cancel or change a booking?

You can cancel free of charge up to [24 hours] before the booked time. If you cancel later, the partner may charge a cancellation fee, which is shown when you book. Recovery jobs that are already under way cannot be cancelled free of charge.

To change a time, contact the partner using the details in your booking, or contact us.

What if the partner cancels or does not turn up?

If the partner cancels, we refund the booking fee and help you find another partner. If someone does not arrive, contact us straight away and we will step in.

Do I need to be there while the work is done?

For mobile work, someone needs to hand over the keys and be available when the job is finished. You do not have to stand with the vehicle. The partner needs safe, legal space to work, such as a driveway or a private car park.

Do I need an account?

You can check prices without one. A free account lets you see exact prices, make bookings and keep your bookings, invoices and messages in one place under My account.

Trust and quality

How do you check your partners?

We check every partner’s photo ID, trade insurance and public liability insurance before they can take a booking, and again when documents expire. These checks help keep the marketplace safe, but they are not a guarantee of the quality of any work.

Is the work guaranteed?

The partner who does the work gives the warranty on their work and the parts they supply. Their warranty terms are shown before you book. Your rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 also apply.

What if something goes wrong?

Contact the partner first, using the details in your booking. If it is not sorted, contact us and we will help both sides reach a fair outcome. Your legal rights are not affected.

Are the reviews real?

Reviews can only be left after a real, completed booking or purchase. We remove reviews that are false, offensive or unlawful.

Services

Which MOT do I need, and what does it cost?

It depends on your vehicle. Most cars, motorhomes, taxis and vans up to 3,000kg are class 4. Motorcycles are class 1 or 2, three-wheelers up to 450kg are class 3, minibuses with 13 or more seats are class 5, and larger vans from 3,000kg to 3,500kg are class 7. Vehicles with 9 or more seats may also need a seat belt installation check (class 4a or 5a).

Choose your MOT type when you book and we show the partner test centres near you. The price is the official maximum fee for the class: for example £54.85 for a car and £29.65 for a motorcycle, with no extra booking fee. You pick a free time from the test centre’s live diary and pay when you book.

Can a mobile mechanic do an MOT?

No. An MOT must be done at an approved test station. Choose MOT, pick your type of MOT, and book at a partner test station.

I have lost my car keys or locked them in the car. Can you help?

Yes. Choose Auto electrician and locksmith. A vehicle locksmith can open the car without damage, cut and program a new key or fob, and wipe lost keys from the car’s memory. They will ask for proof that the vehicle is yours.

My electric car has run out of charge. What can you do?

Choose Mobile EV charging. A charging van comes to you and gives you enough charge to reach a charger or get home. If the car cannot be charged where it is, choose Recovery instead.

Do you repair vans as well as cars?

Yes. Enter the van’s registration and we show partners who work on light commercial vehicles.

I have broken down. What should I do?

Get yourself and any passengers somewhere safe first. If you are in danger on a motorway or a fast road, call 999. Then choose Recovery on the home page to see the price and arrival time before you book.

For cover before you break down, see breakdown cover.

Do you sell breakdown cover?

We help you compare RAC cover levels. You then buy the policy direct from the RAC, and your cover is with them.

Cars and vans for sale

Who am I buying from?

Cars and vans are advertised and sold by independent dealers. Any sale, deposit, part exchange, finance or delivery is agreed between you and the dealer. Motoring Central does not own, inspect or sell the vehicles.

What should I check before I buy?

We recommend you view and test drive the vehicle, check the V5C and the service history, and run a vehicle history check before paying a deposit.

Can I sell my own car or van here?

Yes. A private advert costs £29.99 including VAT and runs for 30 days. There is no commission when it sells. For another £14.99 you can make it a premium advert, shown on the front-page banner for 2 weeks or until sold.

You need a free customer account. Tap “Sell a car or van” on the home page. Your advert is marked Private sale, and buyers message you through the site unless you choose to show your phone number.

What does “Private sale” mean when I am buying?

The car is being sold by a private person, not a dealer. The car must be as described and the seller must have the right to sell it, but there is no dealer warranty and you have fewer rights than when you buy from a business.

See the car in person, check the V5C log book matches the seller, check the MOT history on GOV.UK, and never send money before you have seen the car. You can also book one of our mobile mechanics to inspect it.

Can I pay monthly for a car (car finance)?

We do not arrange car finance ourselves at the moment. Many dealers offer it, so send the dealer a message from the advert and ask what they can do.

Any finance is agreed between you and the dealer or their lender, not with The Motoring Central.

Are adverts checked before they go live?

Yes. Every car and van advert is checked before buyers can see it, usually within a few hours. We look at the photos, price, mileage, description and the vehicle history check, and we watch for common scams such as requests for a deposit or delivery by courier. If we cannot approve an advert, we tell the seller why so they can fix it.

Are cars and vans on the site history checked?

Almost all are. Every private advert, and every dealer advert after the dealer’s 30-day free trial, is checked for outstanding finance, insurance write-off and stolen records before the advert goes live. The result is shown on the advert, and the seller cannot change it.

A dealer in their 30-day free trial who has used the 3 checks it includes can choose to list without a check. Those adverts are clearly marked “Not history checked”, the dealer must still tell us whether the vehicle has been a write-off, and you can still check its MOT history and recorded mileage free from the DVSA (the advert links to it). Ask the dealer for a history check before you buy.

We do not list vehicles reported stolen, scrapped, or recorded as Category A or B write-offs. Private sellers cannot list a car that still has finance on it.

What is an insurance write-off?

When an insurer decides a damaged vehicle is not worth repairing, it is recorded as a write-off. Category S (structural damage) and Category N (damage that was not structural) can be repaired and driven again. Older vehicles may show Category C or D, used before October 2017.

Every write-off we know about is shown in red on the advert, whether the seller told us or our history check found it. A repaired write-off can be a fair buy, but it is usually worth less, some insurers charge more, and you should have it inspected before you buy. Use the filter to hide write-offs if you prefer.

Do prices include VAT?

Car prices are the full price to pay unless the advert says “+ VAT”. Most van prices are shown before VAT. Wherever a price is “+ VAT”, the price including VAT is shown straight underneath, so you can always see what you will actually pay.

The seller chooses this when they list the vehicle. Dealers and VAT-registered businesses selling their own vehicle can list a price + VAT; private individuals cannot charge VAT.

For partners and dealers

How do I join as a partner?

Go to Join the network, choose your trade and apply. We check your photo ID and insurance, and then you can start taking bookings.

What does it cost partners?

You set your own prices. Partners pay one flat fee of [10%] plus VAT per completed job, with no monthly fee. Dealers get their first [3] months free. VAT is added to all our fees to partners, including the per-job fee. Full details are on the network page and in the terms.

How do dealers add vehicles, and is the look-up free?

In the stock system, enter the registration and a look-up fills in the make, model, year, fuel, gearbox, body style, colour and MOT date. Look-ups are free, and you can always type or edit the details yourself. Each vehicle can have up to 30 photos.

How do I advertise a job?

Partners can post a vacancy on the Work in the motor trade page for £9.99 plus VAT. The advert runs for 90 days and applications come straight to you. Searching and applying is free for everyone.

When do partners get paid?

The customer pays when they book. After the job is completed, we pay you what you charged, less our fee. Payment timings are shown in your partner dashboard.

Still need help?

Our UK team is happy to answer anything not covered here. Contact us

Privacy policy

What personal information we collect, why we collect it, who we share it with and the rights you have over it.

Draft for review. This policy is a working draft for the preview site. Have it checked by a solicitor or data protection adviser before launch, and fill in the items in [square brackets]. It must match what the live site and its suppliers really do.

The short version

  • We collect only what we need to give you prices, make your booking, pass an enquiry to a dealer and run your account.
  • We share your details with the partner or dealer you choose, so they can do the job or reply to you.
  • We do not sell your personal information.
  • We send marketing only if you have agreed, and you can stop it at any time.
  • You can ask to see, correct or delete your information. Email privacy@motoringcentral.co.uk.

Tap a section to read it in full. Last updated: [date].

1. Who we are

Motoring Central is run by [The Motoring Central Ltd], a company registered in England and Wales, company number [00000000], registered office [address]. We are the “controller” of the personal information described in this policy.

We are registered with the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), registration number [ZA000000].

For any privacy question, email privacy@motoringcentral.co.uk or write to us at the address above.

2. The information we collect

Information you give us

Your name, email address, phone number, postcode and address; your vehicle registration and details about the job you need; messages you send to us, partners or dealers; reviews you write; and your account log-in details.

Information about your vehicle

When you enter a registration, we look up the make, model, engine, fuel type and similar details from [vehicle data provider], so we can match parts and prices.

Payment information

Card payments are handled by [payment provider]. We receive confirmation of the payment and the last four digits of your card. We do not see or store your full card number.

Information we collect automatically

Technical details such as your device and browser type, IP address and the pages you visit. See our cookie notice.

If you are a partner or dealer

Your business details, photo ID, insurance documents, qualifications, bank details for payouts, your prices and availability, and records of the jobs or adverts you handle.

3. How we use it and our legal basis

UK data protection law requires us to have a legal basis for using your information. We rely on these:

To carry out our contract with you

Showing prices, making and managing bookings, taking payment, passing enquiries to dealers, running your account, and sending service messages such as confirmations and arrival times.

Our legitimate interests

Checking partners and keeping the marketplace safe, preventing fraud, handling complaints, improving our service, and keeping records of what happened on a booking. We make sure these interests do not override your rights.

Legal obligations

Keeping tax and accounting records, and responding to lawful requests from authorities.

Your consent

Marketing emails and texts, and optional cookies. You can withdraw consent at any time.

4. Who we share it with

The partner you book. We give the garage, mechanic, auto electrician, locksmith, body shop, wheel specialist, tyre fitter, valeter, recovery or EV charging company you choose your name, contact details, vehicle details, job details and the address for the work.

The dealer you contact. When you send an enquiry about a car or van, we pass your name, contact details and message to that dealer.

Suppliers who help us run the service, under contract and only for that purpose: [payment provider], [vehicle data provider], [parts supplier], [email and text message provider], [website hosting provider] and [analytics provider].

Maps and postcodes. When you ask for recovery or mobile EV charging, we look up the postcode or location you give with postcodes.io and show it on a map from OpenStreetMap. Those services see the postcode or the area of the map being shown, and your device's internet address, but not your name or booking. Your location is only read from your device if you tap Use my location and allow it.

The RAC. If you follow a link to buy breakdown cover, you buy direct from the RAC and their privacy policy applies to what you give them.

Where your account is kept. Your account details, bookings and messages are stored in a secure database run for us by Supabase, on servers in London. Your password is stored in a scrambled form that we cannot read. Partners' and dealers' insurance certificates and photo ID are kept in private storage there, and can only be opened by that partner and by our staff who check applications.

Postcode look-up. When you type a postcode to see how far away a car or van is, that postcode is sent to Postcodes.io, a look-up service run by Ideal Postcodes, to find where it is. Nothing else about you is sent with it.

Voice search. If you tap the microphone in the search box, your own browser (for example Google Chrome or Apple Safari) turns your speech into text using its speech service. We do not record or keep the sound of your voice.

Authorities and advisers, where the law requires it or to protect our legal rights.

Partners and dealers are independent businesses. They are responsible for how they use your information once they have it, and must use it only to carry out your booking or reply to your enquiry.

5. How long we keep it

Booking, payment and invoice records: [6 years], to meet tax and legal requirements.

Your account: for as long as it is open. If you close it, we delete or anonymise your details within [30 days], apart from records we must keep by law.

Enquiries that do not lead to a booking: [12 months].

Partner and dealer documents: for the length of the membership and [6 years] afterwards.

6. Where it is stored

We store your information in the UK or [European Economic Area]. If a supplier processes it elsewhere, we make sure the legally required safeguards are in place.

We protect your information with measures such as encryption in transit, restricted staff access and partner accounts that only show the bookings they are handling.

7. Your rights

Under UK data protection law you can ask us to:

  • give you a copy of your information;
  • correct anything that is wrong;
  • delete your information, where we no longer need it;
  • restrict or stop certain uses, including all marketing;
  • move your information to another service.

To use any of these rights, email privacy@motoringcentral.co.uk. We will reply within one month. There is normally no charge.

If you are unhappy with how we have handled your information, please tell us first. You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

8. Marketing

We send offers and news only if you have agreed, or if you are an existing customer and did not opt out when we collected your details. Every message has an unsubscribe link, and you can change your choice in My account. Service messages about a booking are not marketing and are always sent.

9. Children

Motoring Central is for people aged 18 or over. We do not knowingly collect information from children.

10. Changes to this policy

We will update this page when what we do changes, and show the date at the top. If a change is significant, we will tell you by email or on the site.

Cookie notice

What cookies and similar storage this site uses, and how to change your choice.

Draft for review. The list below must match the cookies the live site really sets. Review it once hosting, payments and analytics are chosen, and fill in the items in [square brackets].

Your choice

You can change this at any time by coming back to this page from the link at the bottom of every page.

What cookies are

Cookies are small files a website saves on your phone or computer. Sites also use similar browser storage. They let a site remember you between pages, such as keeping you logged in. This notice covers both.

What we use

Essential

Always on

Needed for the site to work, so they do not need your consent.

NameWhat it doesHow long
mc-cookiesRemembers your cookie choice[12 months]
mc-hubKeeps your chats, booking alerts and job status on this device[Until you clear it]
[session]Keeps you logged in to your account or partner dashboard[Until you log out]
[checkout]Set by [payment provider] to take card payments securely and prevent fraud[Set by provider]

Analytics

Optional

Help us see which pages are used and where people get stuck, so we can improve the site. Only set if you choose “Accept all cookies”.

NameWhat it doesHow long
mc-activityOur own count of the pages you view and the buttons you press on this site. If you are logged in, it is linked to your account so we can help you and improve the service. We never record what you type[Up to 13 months]
[analytics]Counts visits and pages viewed, set by [analytics provider][Up to 13 months]

Advertising

We do not use advertising or tracking cookies that follow you to other websites. If that ever changes, we will update this notice and ask for your consent first.

Other ways to control cookies

You can also block or delete cookies in your browser settings. If you block essential cookies, parts of the site such as logging in and booking will not work.

For more about how we use personal information, see our privacy policy.
